feature: The Layers panel knows a group is a row or a column
summary: You can stack picked layers from the Layers panel menu or a row's right-click menu, and the Layers list now says under each name what auto layout does: row, column or grid on the stack, and hug, fill or fixed on each piece inside it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: layers-rows-say-row-or-column-walk and layers-rows-stack-by-right-click-walk.

try.do: Draw two rectangles side by side and type a short label after them.
Pick all three in the Layers list, then choose Stack Selection, the first row of the three dots menu on the Layers header.
Open the new group's twist and read the words under each name: row on the group, fixed on the boxes, hug on the label.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Switch to light mode and read the same words.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Undo, pick two layers again and right click one of their rows: Stack Selection sits under Group, on Control Command G.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Change the stack's Direction to Column in the Layout section and watch the group's word follow.
Group some layers with Command G instead: those rows say nothing about layout.

evaluate: Can you read how a stack is built from the Layers list alone, without picking each piece?
Is the small mono word under the name quiet enough, or does it compete with the name?
Does Stack Selection belong first in the Layers menu, above Group Selection, as the mock has it?
Is 'fixed' the right word for a picture or a shape inside a stack, or would 'size' or nothing read better?
rough: The mock's panel row reads 'Wrap in auto-layout' on Shift A; the app says 'Stack Selection' on Control Command G, the menu bar's own name and key. Your call on card the-layers-list-says-stack-words-the-way-the-aut-how-should-the-layers-panel-name.

The mock prints the word at the row's right end; the app prints it under the name, where every other row note goes. Your call on card the-layers-list-says-stack-words-the-way-the-aut-how-should-the-layers-panel-name.
The mock turns a picked row's word accent; here it stays grey, because nine points of accent over the row's accent wash is not reliably legible (your rule on 2026-09-30: text is always legible).
Pieces of a grid say nothing, since a cell decides their size; the mock draws no grid, so nothing there to match.
A surface stretched behind a stack, or a piece floated in front, says nothing either: it is not one of the pieces the stack lines up.
